items.summary: A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice to the Election Commission of India, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on the SIR writ petition W.P.(C) 001351/2026 filed Oct 12 by Rahul Gandhi and 12 other INDIA-bloc leaders (Kharge, Saugata Roy, Akhilesh Yadav, Tejashwi Yadav, Sanjay Raut, MA Baby, D Raja, Mahua Majhi, Supriya Sule, ET Mohammed Basheer, plus Thol. Thirumavalavan and Sajjad Kichloo who joined later). The plea challenges voter deletions and SIR irregularities and seeks ECI files, minutes, notings and ECINET/ERONET records. The court tagged it with pending SIR matters and made it returnable October 27.
items.title: SC issues notice to ECI on INDIA-bloc SIR writ; returnable Oct 27

items.summary: While entertaining the INDIA-bloc petition, the CJI-led bench ordered that the petition 'on behalf of Petitioner No. 6' (Shiv Sena-UBT MP Sanjay Raut) is entertained on a provisional basis, subject to his explaining his conduct. Raut had alleged the CJI and judges played badminton in London with BJP leaders and attended dinners with BJP ministers while declining a meeting with Rahul Gandhi. Attorney General R. Venkataramani had granted consent on Oct 14 to the Supreme Court Bar Association to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against Raut, calling the badminton claim false (citing a Delhi HC order) and the remarks scandalous. The CJI remarked the judges are 'not sitting in ivory towers' and are aware of statements made outside the courtroom.
items.title: SC asks Sanjay Raut to explain remarks against CJI, judges; AG cleared contempt route

items.summary: Other outcomes from the Oct-15 hearing before CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi: (1) Notice issued on the four-advocates' plea seeking safeguards against political demonstrations at court premises after the Oct-12 INDIA-bloc march; CJI: 'nobody can browbeat us'; Justice Bagchi ordered preservation of CCTV and digital footage of the march; an allegation that Rahul Gandhi pushed a woman journalist was raised by Gaurav Bhatia. (2) Notice issued on the challenge to BNSS Section 172, which the bench described as 'a preventive detention provision'; nodal counsel to identify overlapping issues. (3) Protection for a woman journalist and backing for a women-led panel on Delhi protest complaints (NWMI/Indira Jaising, Free Speech Collective contempt plea, Kerala Union of Working Journalists Article 32 plea). (4) The bench declined to take cognizance of the authorities' 'unqualified apology', with Justice Bagchi noting the SG's submissions made it a qualified apology. (5) The court agreed to examine a separate plea challenging the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a protest site.
items.title: SC Oct-15 hearing: notice on Oct-12 march plea, Sec 172 BNSS notice, journalist protections

items.event_time_ist: Oct 15 (orders and HC hearing); march today 5 PM IST, Oct 16
items.summary: Ahead of today's 5 PM 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Connaught Place's Central Park: NDMC closed Central Park to the public on Oct 16-17 for 'administrative reasons'; Delhi Police imposed Section 163 BNSS in CP and asked the public to stay away, offering only a select 'group of 11' at an alternate location for flag-waving and the anthem; DCP PRO Neha Yadav cited traders' letters seeking protection; traders/vendors warned of a counter-protest if they lose another festive-season weekend. The Delhi High Court on Thursday (Acting CJ Nitin Wasudeo Sambre + Justice Sanjay Sharma) refused to restrain CJP/Dipke from protesting, taking on record the police's assurance (ASG Chetan Sharma) that all regulatory steps would be taken. Delhi Police told the HC the Jantar Mantar denotification was on the Supreme Court's directions and the court suggested spacious alternative venues (The Hindu). Deployment: 6,000 Delhi Police + 220 CAPF companies + expanded CCTV; traffic advisory restricts 20 roads around CP from 3 PM. AAP has extended support and is mobilising for the march.
items.title: Tiranga march eve: NDMC shuts Central Park 2 days, Sec 163 in CP, HC refuses to restrain protest

items.summary: At a Thursday press conference, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged that vehicles without number plates are following him and Intelligence Bureau officials are monitoring his residence, and said Delhi Police could detain him Thursday night or Friday morning ahead of the Tiranga march. 'If we have to go to jail to wave the Tiranga in this country, then we are ready for it,' he said, adding: 'If we announce 100 places, will Narendra Modi shut down all 100 places?' In Friday's live coverage he asked, 'Why is PM Modi locking down Delhi to shield one individual?' Aaj Tak's graphic quoted him saying 'Police can take me into custody.' The surveillance claims are his own allegations, not independently corroborated.
items.title: Dipke alleges IB surveillance ahead of Tiranga march, says 'ready to go to jail'

items.summary: At a Thursday press conference, the Cockroach Janta Party announced a nationwide mobilisation campaign against the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls starting October 23. The party said it would take its campaign directly to states with upcoming elections to collect evidence of alleged voter-list irregularities, reiterated its demand for CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal, and said farmers, Dalits, students and Gen Z youth would participate. The party also said it has already submitted evidence to the panel hearing the SIR-related case.
items.title: CJP announces nationwide SIR campaign from Oct 23
